correctness.rationale: For an adjacent pair with angular gap less than pi, the two inequalities are exactly a positive cone representation of the polygonal edge as nonnegative multiples of the rotated endpoint normals. Projection monotonicity proves all omitted inequalities from nearest neighbours, using a closed circular chain for positive-spanning directions and an open monotone chain in a semicircle. Perturbed circumscribed polygons provide configurations with exactly one active original inequality for every retained facet, also after auxiliary-normals insertion across a large gap. A strict interior point and exact translation-lineality argument finish the classification. The 15,514 LP checks on 378 configurations corroborate but are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The same natural vertex-normal parameter cone arises as a concrete finite-dimensional representation space for convex-body approximation. Replacing N(N−1) constraints by a provably minimal 2N or 2N−2 constraints cuts the exact H-description from quadratic to linear size while preserving every degenerate boundary configuration. The sharp angular threshold and all-facet result resolve the motivating gap between individual redundancy and safe simultaneous removal; this has both structural and algorithmic significance.
